title: Throwing Initialisers vs Failable
hints: `init?` can only say "no"; a throwing init can say *why*.
Validate in the throwing init; the failable init can call it with `try?` and assign `self`.
`guard let email = try? Email(validating: raw) else { return nil }; self = email`.
jsBridge: `init?` returns `nil` on bad input, and `init() throws` explains *why*. JS constructors can only throw, so the "return nil" option is Swift-specific and ideal when the caller doesn't care about the reason.

compass.q: JS constructors can't return null. Would you rather have `Email.parse()` return null or throw? How does Swift let the caller choose?
`init?` vs `init() throws` vs a static `validate() -> Result`: which gives the best form UX?
Can a failable init delegate to a throwing init? With `try?`?
`URL(string:)` is failable, while `JSONDecoder().decode` throws. Why did Apple choose differently?
